lines.say: Start in 2010, with house prices in Germany, Portugal and Italy on the same line.
Germany climbs steadily. Portugal dips at first, then takes off. Italy slides.
By 2019, the average Italian home is worth 17 percent less than in 2010.
Then prices start rising almost everywhere.
By 2025, German house prices are up 82 percent on 2010. Portugal's, 146 percent. Italy's? Still down 2 percent.
Fifteen years, and an Italian home is worth a little less than when it started, before inflation.
Where prices exploded instead: our full video on 28 November.
